question.problem: Suppose $f(x)=a{x}^{2}+bx-10$ has a factor of $x+2$ and has a remainder of $18$ when divided by $x+4.$ Find the value of $a+b.$
question.worked_solution:
Since $(x+2)$ is a factor of $f(x)$, it must divide into $f(x)$ with no remainder. In other words, when $f(x)$ is divided by $(x+2),$ the remainder is $0.$ It follows from the remainder theorem that

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & =f(-2) \\  & =a(-2)^{2}+b(-2)-10 \\  & =a(4)+b(-2)-10 \\  & =4a-2b-10.\end{aligned}
$$

Likewise, since we're told that the remainder is $18$ when $f(x)$ is divided by $(x+4),$ it follows from the remainder theorem that

$$
\begin{aligned}18 & =f(-4) \\  & =a(-4)^{2}+b(-4)-10 \\  & =a(16)+b(-4)-10 \\  & =16a-4b-10.\end{aligned}
$$

We now have the system of equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}0=4a-2b-10 \\ 18=16a-4b-10.\end{aligned}
$$

Simplifying each equation, we get

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2a-b=5 \\ 4a-b=7.\end{aligned}
$$

To eliminate $a,$ we subtract the equations and get

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & a-b &  & =7 \\ -\,2 & a-b &  & =5 \\ 2 & a &  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get $2a=2,$ and hence $a=1.$ Finally, we substitute it into $2a-b=5$ to find $b=-3.$ 

Therefore, our final solution is $(a,b)=(1,-3).$ 

Finally then, $a+b=1-3=-2$
